notes: Slightly reduced lateral sensor spacing by shifting sensors inward by 0.01 m to test if a more concentrated sensor array improves line detection continuity through sharp turns on the slalom track. Maintained sixth center-front sensor and sensor size for early detection benefits. Controller keeps kp at 6 for smooth steering. Observation requests cover key performance metrics.
rationale: The previous iteration's evidence shows that increasing sensor size to 0.016 m, adding a sixth center-front sensor, and expanding lateral sensor spacing improved line coverage and early detection, reducing line loss events on oval and s-bend tracks. However, the slalom track still has zero finish rate and relatively high steering oscillation, indicating challenges with sharp turns and control stability. To address this, I slightly reduce the lateral spacing by shifting sensors inward by 0.01 m to create a more concentrated sensor array, aiming to improve line detection continuity through sharp turns. The sixth center-front sensor and sensor size remain unchanged to preserve early detection benefits. The controller keeps the reduced kp of 6 to maintain smooth steering and low oscillation. Other geometry parameters remain unchanged for stability. I expect this fine-tuning of sensor lateral positions to reduce line loss events and steering oscillation on the slalom track, while maintaining strong performance on oval and s-bend tracks.
